{{nihongo|'''Yahagi Shrine, Yao'''|矢作神社 (八尾市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Yahagi Shrine''' (やはぎじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Minamihonmachi, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank in the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

It is also called "'''Betsugū Hachiman'''," and "Yahagi" is also read as "Yatsukuri."

=== Overview ===
This area is said to have originally been the residence site of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yahagi no Muraji}}, a collateral branch of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}, and the shrine is their tutelary shrine.

In the 11th century it became a Kamo-betsugū (Yao Kamo-betsugū) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}}, and in the Edo period it performed Kamo service duties for Iwashimizu Hachiman-gū. This is why it is called Betsugū Hachiman.

Several large {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}} grow in the precincts. In addition, a large {{ill|Ginkgo biloba|Q43284|qid=Q43284|lt=ichō}} tree in front of the shrine has many breast-like protrusions on its trunk, and there is a folk belief that decocting and drinking this bark increases breast milk.

The shrine preserves a "{{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|Q11357232|qid=Q11357232}}" mirror said to have been excavated from the precincts, designated a Yao City tangible cultural property.
